body.en: The Securities and Exchange Board of India was set up in 1988 and given statutory powers in 1992. Its objectives are to protect the interests of investors, to promote the development of the securities market and to regulate it. It registers and regulates stock exchanges, brokers, merchant bankers, depositories, mutual funds and credit rating agencies; prohibits fraudulent and unfair trade practices and insider trading; regulates take-overs; and promotes investor education.

points.en: Protective: investors, against fraud and insider trading
Developmental: training, investor education, new products

title.en: Net asset value of a mutual fund

caption.en: A mutual fund pools investors' money and invests it in shares and bonds. Its net asset value (NAV) per unit is the value of its assets less its liabilities, divided by the number of units. Change the market value and see what an investor's units are worth.

title.en: On the board: SEBI's three roles

say.en: SEBI's functions fall into three groups.

text.en: Protective: stop insider trading and fraud

body.en: A stock exchange provides a regulated place (now electronic) where securities are bought and sold. Stock brokers are registered members who trade on behalf of investors. Merchant bankers manage public issues: they plan the issue, prepare the offer document and coordinate with other agencies. Depositories (NSDL and CDSL) hold securities in electronic (dematerialised) form, and investors deal through depository participants. Mutual funds pool money from many investors and invest it through professional fund managers; investors hold units whose value is the NAV. Credit rating agencies such as CRISIL, ICRA and CARE assess the ability of a borrower to repay debt and give ratings.

points.en: Stock exchange: market place for securities
Depositories: hold securities in demat form
Mutual funds and credit rating agencies
